title.narrative: Life-saving water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) and child protection supplies and services to typhoon Yagi affected populations in Myanmar

description.narrative: The Child Protection Programme will prioritize displaced populations—children, adolescents, and parents/caregivers—in flood-affected communities in Mandalay and Southern Shan. In collaboration with local organizations, the programme will provide a comprehensive package of life-saving child protection services to 10,065 people. These services will include mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), age- and gender-sensitive case management, and referrals for at-risk children. Additionally, it will offer victim assistance for children affected by explosive ordnance, family tracing and reunification (FTR) for separated and unaccompanied children, and awareness campaigns on key child protection messages, explosive ordnance risks, gender-based violence (GBV) prevention, and protection from sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA).In addition, UNICEF aims to improve access to water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) for 25,000 people affected by the floods through several initiatives. These efforts will include: 1) distributing water purification supplies such as tablets and flocculants, providing water filters and storage containers, and delivering water through trucking and installing storage tanks; 2) constructing or restoring sanitation facilities, including communal and household latrines with handwashing stations, as well as communal bathing facilities; 3) distributing essential WASH supplies such as family hygiene kits and menstrual hygiene products, paired with hygiene promotion to encourage better WASH practices; and 4) restoring and improving WASH services in schools and learning spaces.
